must_remember: The NOT gate inverts a single input terminal producing $Y = \overline{A}$.
The AND gate yields a HIGH output only when all inputs are HIGH ($Y = A \cdot B$).
The OR gate yields a HIGH output if at least one input is HIGH ($Y = A + B$).
NAND and NOR gates are universal gates because any boolean function can be realized using only one type of gate.
The XOR gate acts as an odd-bit detector and binary adder component with $Y = \overline{A}B + A\overline{B}$.
The XNOR gate functions as an equality detector yielding HIGH when all inputs are identical ($Y = AB + \overline{A}\overline{B}$).
De Morgan's laws state that $\overline{A + B} = \overline{A} \cdot \overline{B}$ and $\overline{A \cdot B} = \overline{A} + \overline{B}$.
A combinational logic circuit with $n$ inputs requires $N_{rows} = 2^{n}$ rows in its truth table.

glossary.meaning: An inverter logic gate that takes a single binary input and produces its complement as output.
A logic gate that produces a HIGH output if and only if all inputs are HIGH.
A logic gate that produces a HIGH output if one or more inputs are HIGH.
A logic gate (such as NAND or NOR) that can implement any Boolean function without needing any other gate type.
Exclusive-OR gate producing a HIGH output when an odd number of inputs are HIGH.
Exclusive-NOR gate acting as an equality detector, producing HIGH when inputs match.
Fundamental Boolean algebra theorems relating logical operations of AND, OR, and NOT.
